Reading a Roman Monument

A close-looking exercise for ARH 2050, Chapter 7 (The Roman Empire). Study three details cut into this one monument first, then step back to see the whole structure.

Photograph: south facade, Arch of Constantine, Rome (312–315 CE).

Look first

Spend 30 seconds examining a part of the monument before any context appears. What do you notice about the figures, the carving, or the composition?

30seconds

Tip: use the arrow keys to move between stops. The small inset image in the lower-left corner of the viewer always shows where the current detail sits on the whole monument.
